Using get-review-context (already provided) and building the threat model for EVAL-05 now.

**Summary of findings for EVAL-05 (SSO with corporate IdP):**

The design trusts a SAML role attribute to grant admin access on an internet-facing portal, with no mention of signature/replay validation. Main risks: forged or replayed assertions granting admin, and role-attribute trust enabling privilege escalation.

I'll submit the full threat model now.

      "title": "Forged SAML assertion grants admin access",
      "scenario": "An attacker crafts or modifies a SAML assertion claiming an admin role. If the portal does not strictly verify the IdP's XML signature on the assertion (including signature wrapping defenses), the attacker is logged in as an administrator of the internet-facing portal without ever authenticating to the real IdP.",

      "plainLanguage": "Someone could fake or tamper with the SSO login message and tell the portal they're an admin.",

        "title": "Validate SAML assertion signatures and structure before trusting claims",
        "given": "A SAML response is received from the IdP",
        "when": "The portal processes the assertion",
        "then": "It must cryptographically verify the signature covers the whole assertion, reject unsigned or wrapped assertions, and validate issuer/audience before reading any attribute"

      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Role attribute from IdP blindly trusted for admin decision",
      "scenario": "The portal grants admin solely based on a role attribute inside the SAML assertion. If that attribute can be influenced (e.g. a misconfigured IdP group mapping, a shared/self-service attribute, or an unexpected default value for unmapped users), a regular employee ends up with admin rights on the internet-reachable portal with no additional authorization check.",
      "component": "Role attribute parser",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [{"quote": "After login, the portal reads the role attribute from the assertion to decide admin access."}],
      "asvs": ["V8.3.4"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-269", "CWE-285"],
      "plainLanguage": "The app decides who's an admin just from a label sent by the login system, with no second check.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Enforce server-side authorization independent of IdP attribute",
        "given": "A user authenticates via SSO with a role attribute",
        "when": "The portal grants admin-level access",
        "then": "It must cross-check the claimed role against an authoritative, portal-controlled admin allowlist, not rely solely on the assertion attribute"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "SAML assertion replay due to missing anti-replay checks",
      "scenario": "An attacker who intercepts or obtains a valid SAML assertion (e.g. via a shared/public network, browser history, or logs) replays it against the internet-facing portal. Without validation of InResponseTo, assertion recipient/audience, one-time-use markers, and a tight NotOnOrAfter window, the attacker reuses the captured assertion to log in as the original employee, including admins.",
      "component": "SAML SSO flow",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [{"quote": "Employees sign in to the internal admin portal through SAML single sign-on with the corporate identity provider."}, {"quote": "The portal is reachable from the internet."}],
      "asvs": ["V3.5.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-294"],
      "plainLanguage": "A copied login proof could be reused later by an attacker to sign in as someone else.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Reject replayed or expired SAML assertions",
        "given": "A SAML assertion is submitted to the portal",
        "when": "It is processed for login",
        "then": "The portal must validate InResponseTo, audience restriction, a short validity window, and reject any assertion ID already consumed"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Internet exposure of admin portal widens SSO attack surface",
      "scenario": "The admin portal is designed to be used by internal employees but is reachable from the internet, with the only gate being SSO login success and the role check. Any flaw or misconfiguration in the SAML flow (signature bypass, replay, assertion confusion) is directly exploitable by any internet attacker rather than requiring internal network access first, removing a defense-in-depth layer.",
      "component": "Internal admin portal",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [{"quote": "The portal is reachable from the internet."}],
      "asvs": ["V1.1.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-284"],
      "plainLanguage": "An admin-only internal tool can be reached by anyone on the internet, so any login flaw is attackable by strangers, not just insiders.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Restrict exposure of internal admin functionality",
        "given": "The admin portal is intended for internal employee use",
        "when": "It is deployed to be internet-reachable",
        "then": "Access must be additionally restricted (e.g. VPN, IP allowlist, or network-level control) so SSO is not the sole barrier between the internet and admin functions"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "No traceable link between SSO identity and admin actions",
      "scenario": "Because admin access is granted purely by reading a role attribute at login time, if that attribute or the user's underlying IdP identity is later found to be compromised or incorrectly mapped, there is nothing described that ties each admin action back to a verified, immutable identity assertion, making it hard to establish who actually performed a given administrative action.",
      "component": "Internal admin portal",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [{"quote": "After login, the portal reads the role attribute from the assertion to decide admin access."}],
      "asvs": ["V7.3.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "If an admin account turns out to be fake or miscategorized, it may be hard to prove who really did what.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Bind admin actions to a stable verified identity claim",
        "given": "A user is granted admin access via SSO role attribute",
        "when": "They perform administrative actions",
        "then": "The portal must record the IdP subject identifier and assertion ID used to authenticate alongside each privileged action"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Submitting this now.
